note.headline: Equities slip on narrow breadth while commodities rally and curve flattens
note.standfirst: The S&P fell -0.58% on the thinnest breadth of the week, eight advancers against sixteen decliners, as oil, copper and the ag complex rallied against a flattening front end of the Treasury curve. The setup argues for an inflation repricing rather than a growth scare, and 2s10s at 41bp is the level that decides which one it is.
takeaways: Breadth was thin: eight advancers against sixteen decliners, a ratio of 0.50, even as the S&P held to a -0.58% loss.
The curve flattened as the front end sold off, 2yr yields +3bp to 4.37% and 30yr yields -1bp to 5.24%, while breakevens rose across every tenor.
Commodities rallied broadly: WTI +3.02%, copper +2.67% to a fresh high, with corn and soybeans also printing highs.
Health care was the weak sector at -2.52% while tech held near flat, a split visible inside the leaders and laggards list: AMD +5.90% and Broadcom +2.98% against Nvidia -2.01%.
note.desk_view:
The standard risk-off script, stocks and yields falling together, did not show up today. Equities fell (S&P -0.58%, Dow -1.18%) while front-end yields rose (2yr +3bp, 3yr +4bp) and the curve flattened, 2s10s to 41bp and 5s30s to 70bp. Breakevens rose across every tenor, 5yr +3bp to 2.40 and 10yr +2bp to 2.37, and the 10yr TIPS real yield added +1bp. Oil rose +3.02%, copper rose +2.67% to a fresh high. That combination reads closer to an inflation repricing than a growth scare. The level that decides it is 2s10s: continued front-end selling against a capped long end extends pressure on the growth-sensitive sectors that already lagged today, health care -2.52% and financials -1.38%. A long end that catches up instead resets the story to a duration scare, one that would not spare the mega-cap tech names currently insulated by AMD, Tesla, Broadcom and Oracle.

The risk barometer read -0.26, "neutral," but that score masked a real split rather than a calm session. USD/JPY was the single largest drag at -3.0, MOVE at -0.87, SPX at -0.84, while copper contributed +1.84 and DXY +1.15. A neutral print built from offsetting extremes is a different market than one built from everything sitting near zero. Breadth of 8 versus 16 and dispersion of 2.1 say the internals were not neutral at all.
watching: Whether 2s10s keeps flattening or the long end catches up to the front-end selloff.
Follow-through in oil and copper after today's rally, a test of the inflation-repricing read.
Whether health care's split holds, UnitedHealth +0.93% against Lilly -2.21% and Pfizer -2.32%.
Whether Asia's divide persists, KOSPI +4.61% and Nikkei +2.12% against CSI 300 -3.60%.
note.equities:
The S&P fell -0.58% to 7673.52, the Dow was the weakest major at -1.18% to 52786.07, and the Nasdaq 100 was flat at -0.12% to 29507.70 as chip and auto names offset broader softness. The Russell 2000 fell -0.52%, the MidCap 400 fell -0.69%, and the NYSE Composite fell -0.67%, so the loss was broad across cap tiers even where the headline index looked calm.

Sector rotation matched the macro story more than the tape's small headline move. Energy led at +1.11% and utilities added +0.86%, both defensive-adjacent or inflation-linked plays, while health care dropped -2.52% and financials fell -1.38%. Technology held at +0.32% on the back of AMD +5.90% and Broadcom +2.98%, but Nvidia fell -2.01%, so the sector average hid real dispersion at the stock level. Breadth of eight advancers against sixteen decliners and dispersion of 2.1 confirm a market where the index number undersold the damage underneath.
note.rates:
The curve flattened, 2s10s down 2bp to 41bp and 5s30s down 3bp to 70bp, driven entirely by the front end. Yields rose from the 2yr through the 10yr, 2yr +3bp to 4.37%, 5yr +2bp to 4.54%, 10yr +1bp to 4.78%, while the 30yr slipped -1bp to 5.24%. The 2yr, 3yr, 5yr and 7yr tenors all sit at highs for the period, and 7-10yr Treasuries (IEF) sit at lows, a split that puts the selling squarely in the belly and front end rather than at the long end.

Breakevens rose across every tenor: 5yr +3bp to 2.40, 10yr +2bp to 2.37, and the 5y5y forward +1bp to 2.34. The 10yr TIPS real yield added +1bp to 2.43. Rising breakevens against a flattening nominal curve is the inflation-repricing signature, not the growth-scare one. MOVE rose +4.16% to 76.143, so rates volatility firmed alongside the yield move rather than fading it.
note.credit: Credit tone was soft but not disorderly. High yield (HYG) fell -0.05%, JNK fell -0.06%, and EM sovereign debt (EMB) fell -0.12%, modest give-back rather than a spread blowout. Investment grade (LQD) was flat on the day at 0.00% but sits at a low for the period, and leveraged loans (BKLN) fell -0.05%. Long Treasuries (TLT) fell -0.01% and 7-10yr Treasuries (IEF) fell -0.10% while also printing a low, consistent with the front-end-led selloff in rates rather than a credit-specific event.
note.fx: The dollar index fell -0.33% to 98.836, but the move was not uniform against G10. The euro rose +0.13%, sterling rose +0.17%, and the Australian dollar rose +0.19% to a high for the period, while the Canadian dollar strengthened -0.36% against the greenback. USD/JPY was the standout, down -1.57% to 153.745, the largest single move in the G10 bloc and the biggest drag on the day's risk barometer. In EM, the Brazilian real strengthened -0.77% against the dollar, the Mexican peso weakened +0.13% while USD/MXN still sits at a low for the period, and USD/TRY rose +0.07% to a fresh high.
note.commodities: Energy and industrial metals led a broad commodity rally. WTI rose +3.02% to 94.24 and Brent rose +3.22% to 99.38, while copper rose +2.67% to 6.773, a fresh high. Gold fell -0.72% to 4398.1 even as silver rose +0.27%, an unusual split between the two precious metals. Aluminium rose +2.18% and the ags moved together, corn +4.05% and soybeans +1.78%, both at highs, alongside wheat +4.37%. Natural gas fell -2.59% and coffee fell -10.58%, the two clear outliers to the broader upside move.
note.volatility: The VIX rose +2.75% to 15.72, still a low absolute level even as the term structure sent a mixed signal: VIX 9-day fell -12.11% and VIX 3-month fell -10.47%, both dropping hard against the spot VIX rise. VVIX rose +5.06% to 88.69 while SKEW fell -1.79% to 148.86, so the cost of tail protection eased even as short-dated realized-vol proxies firmed. MOVE, the rates equivalent, rose +4.16% to 76.143, and that move looks more informative than the equity vol complex given the session's real story sat in the bond market.
note.digital: Digital assets traded with a muted, slightly negative beta to the day's risk tone. Bitcoin fell -0.78% to 78497.97, Ether fell -0.23%, and Solana fell -0.53%, all modest declines that tracked the broader equity weakness without amplifying it. XRP was the exception, up +1.42%, a standalone move against the rest of the complex.
note.international: Asia closed split down the middle. The Nikkei rose +2.12% and the KOSPI rose +4.61%, while the CSI 300 fell -3.60% and the Hang Seng fell -0.93%, so the region handed New York no consistent read on risk appetite. Europe was calmer: the EURO STOXX 50 rose +0.17%, the CAC rose +0.33%, while the DAX slipped -0.15% and the SMI fell -0.81%. Nothing in either session explains the US afternoon's sector split, which leaves the domestic curve move as the more useful cross-check for tomorrow.
note.correlation:
Today's cross-asset picture was defined by a break in the usual stocks-versus-yields relationship rather than a confirmation of it. Equities fell while front-end and belly yields rose, a combination that normally shows up alongside falling risk assets and falling yields together. Instead the move looked like a commodity-and-breakeven story: oil, copper and the grain complex rallied while nominal yields at the front end rose in step with breakevens, and equities were the asset absorbing the adjustment.

A continuation of that pattern, commodities up, front-end yields up, equities soft, would confirm an inflation-driven repricing and put more weight on the sectors already showing stress, health care and financials. A break in it, where the long end sells off alongside the front end or where equities stabilize despite continued commodity strength, would argue the move was a one-day positioning event rather than a regime shift. The 2s10s level at 41bp and the direction of the 30yr from here are the cleanest tells.
